concept_name: Conformations of Ethane: Staggered, Eclipsed, and the Energy of Turning
source_book: NCERT Chemistry Class 11, Ch.13 'Hydrocarbons', §13.2 — alkanes: conformations of ethane, sawhorse and Newman projections — chapter-index scope reference only; teaching sequence, real-world anchor, narration and drill-down phrasings authored from first principles. Every energy carries a primary literature citation stamped on the engine's ORG_ENERGY_TABLE.ethane row: Kemp & Pitzer, JACS 59 (1937) 276; Weiss & Leroi, J. Chem. Phys. 48 (1968) 962 (V3 ≈ 1024 cm⁻¹). NCERT's 12.5 kJ·mol⁻¹ is the 3.0 kcal·mol⁻¹ rounding of the same measurement — reconciled in the barrier_vs_bond_breaking drill-down, never on canvas.

real_world_anchor.primary: A hexagonal pencil lying on a flat table rests on one of its flat faces. Push it and it rolls, but not smoothly — it lifts over an edge and drops onto the next face. It can be turned to any position, yet it is almost always found resting on a face. That is the whole concept in an object every student owns: a rotation that is possible but not free, with resting positions separated by small barriers. It is physics-true rather than metaphorical — a periodic potential in a rotational coordinate, minima at the faces and maxima at the edges. The one honest difference: at room temperature ethane's barrier is small enough that the molecule turns millions of times a second, while the pencil stays put.
real_world_anchor.secondary: The lid of a screw-top bottle turns freely all the way round — the counter-example that sharpens the pencil. Offered as a foil only; the guided narration does not use it.

aha_moment.statement: Rotation about a single bond is not free: the energy rises and falls.
aha_moment.visual_confirmation: the same rotation the student has already watched twice now draws the energy curve as it happens — the rider IS the drawing tip, measured off the turning molecule — and the curve falls three times and climbs three times in one turn

phi_deg.name: dihedral angle about C1-C2, measured C1H1-C1-C2-C2H1

n_fold.name: rotor symmetry number of a methyl group

period_deg.name: period of the torsional energy profile

phi_rate_deg_per_s.name: free-run rate of the dihedral in the explore sandbox (torsion.continuous — the ONE driver of the one visible motion)

constraints: atoms are conserved at every phi: C 2 and H 6 on every frame, no bond made and no bond broken (FIXED)
connectivity is invariant at every phi: exactly 1 C-C bond and 6 C-H bonds, same adjacency (FIXED)
total charge is 0 at every phi; every formal charge is 0 and every carbon oxidation number is -3 (FIXED)
E(phi) = 6(1 + cos 3phi) kJ/mol with phi in degrees, E = 0 at staggered (FIXED, published table; the engine never computes an energy)
barrier = max(E) - min(E) = 12 - 0 = 12 kJ/mol (DERIVED from the published stationary rows, not sampled)
phi is reported wrapped into [0, 360): the explore state's free-run drives phi past 360 and the HUD and the slider handle both roll through 0 rather than clamping at the control's maximum (FIXED)

STATE_1.title: The C–C bond turns
STATE_1.motion_delta: the back methyl turns 68° about the C–C axis in a fixed oblique 3D view, from just past eclipsed through staggered; nothing else moves

scene_composition.describes: ethane: two carbon spheres, six hydrogen spheres, seven drawn bonds, rotating about the C1–C2 axis from φ = 12° to φ = 80°. The camera is the pose at which BOTH acceptance criteria hold at every φ of that sweep — every disc countable (min gap +0.1496) and each carbon reading as a splayed tripod, not a flat T (measured note item 2)
value-only HUD, top-right: 'C 2 · H 6' recounted live from the drawn scene every frame, and 'φ = N.N°' measured on the built geometry
the on-canvas delta cue 'The C–C bond turns' (Rule 34a — prose narration lives in the strip below the canvas)
the φ row, shown but disabled; its handle tracks the MEASURED dihedral off the built geometry and reads 80 at the end of the sweep

misconception_watch.belief: Staggered and eclipsed are different compounds.
misconception_watch.visual_counter: the HUD prints C 2 · H 6 at every instant and no bond ever breaks; one molecule turns continuously from one arrangement into the other without interruption
misconception_watch.one_line_fix: Staggered and eclipsed are the same molecule at different points of one rotation.

tts_sentences.text_en: A hexagonal pencil rolls to any position, yet it rests on a flat face.
Ethane turns the same way about its C–C sigma bond.
The angle φ measures the turn. The count stays the same: two carbons, six hydrogens.

STATE_2.title: Look down the C–C bond
STATE_2.motion_delta: the camera glides from the oblique 3D pose onto the C–C bond axis while the molecule holds a static staggered pose

scene_composition.describes: ethane held static at staggered; as the camera reaches the axis the front carbon becomes the point where three bonds meet and the back carbon is drawn as the Newman rim circle
value-only HUD: 'bond = C1–C2', 'pose = staggered' (static pose, so the line cannot contradict the picture), 'C 2 · H 6'
the on-canvas delta cue 'Now looking down the bond'
the View row, shown but disabled, reading 'Along the bond' — the state's own taught variable, named where the teacher can point at it

misconception_watch.belief: A Newman projection is two overlapping Y shapes; I cannot tell front from back.
misconception_watch.visual_counter: the camera travels from the familiar 3D view onto the bond axis over 12.5 seconds, so the confusing symbol is built in front of the student rather than presented finished
misconception_watch.one_line_fix: The centre point is the front carbon; the circle is the back carbon.

tts_sentences.text_en: The camera moves onto the bond axis. This view is the Newman projection.
The front carbon is the centre point; the back carbon is the circle.
Each sp³ carbon puts its three hydrogens 120° apart.

STATE_3.title: Staggered and eclipsed
STATE_3.motion_delta: the drawn dihedral arc shrinks to nothing as the front hydrogens rotate onto the back ones; the state stops AT eclipsed

scene_composition.describes: ethane in the Newman view at dist 8; the three front hydrogens rotate onto the three back ones, staying countable (measured disc gap +0.198 against the engine's 0.12 floor)

the drawn dihedral arc between the two reference hydrogens, built from their directions projected perpendicular to the C–C bond, with the engine's self-identifying label 'φ(C1–C2) = N.N°' counting 60.0 down to 0.0
the on-canvas delta cue 'Hydrogens line up: eclipsed'
the φ row, shown but disabled; the handle tracks the closing dihedral. The HUD is OFF in this state so the arc label is the only φ string on screen

tts_sentences.text_en: The angle φ starts at 60°, with the hydrogens between each other.
This is the staggered arrangement.
As the bond turns, φ falls to 0° and front and back hydrogens line up: eclipsed.

STATE_4.title: Turning costs energy
STATE_4.motion_delta: the rotation is the pen: the curve grows left to right and the rider rides at its drawing tip, measured off the turning molecule; the turn stops 12° short of the full circle so the pinned molecule is not the pose STATE_3 ended on

scene_composition.describes: ethane in the Newman view, turning through one rotation less 12° and passing eclipsed three times. The 12° is the measured separation floor: at 12° every back hydrogen disc has cleared the position it held at eclipsed, so the pinned frame differs from STATE_3's and STATE_5's in the MOLECULE and not only in the caption (measured note item 6)

the torsional energy curve, revealed over the same window as the sweep so the drawing tip never leads or lags the molecule; axes φ (°) 0→360 and E (kJ·mol⁻¹), stationary points labelled staggered / eclipsed from the published registry row, stamped (literature)

the point riding the curve at the MEASURED dihedral of the molecule on screen — one number drives both, so the rider cannot drift from the pose. It settles 12° (19 px of the 700 px plot, 10 px as displayed) inside the drawn right-hand end
value-only HUD 'E = N.N kJ·mol⁻¹', running 12.0 → 0.0 → 12.0 → 0.0 → 12.0 → 0.0 → 10.9 across the turn (10.9 is E at the settled φ = 348°, on the last climb)
the on-canvas delta cue 'Turning draws an energy curve'
the φ row, shown but disabled; the handle tracks the sweep

misconception_watch.belief: Rotation about a single bond is completely free; it costs nothing.
misconception_watch.visual_counter: the identical rotation the student has already watched twice now draws a curve that rises and falls; the contrast is structural, not staged, and nothing pauses to ask a question
misconception_watch.one_line_fix: Single bonds turn, but not freely — the energy rises and falls as they turn.

tts_sentences.text_en: The same turn now draws an energy curve.
The moving dot is this molecule's own angle.
In one full turn the curve falls three times and climbs three times.
Rotation about a single bond costs energy.

STATE_5.title: The barrier is 12 kJ·mol⁻¹
STATE_5.motion_delta: the curve and its bracket settle first, then the rider alone crosses one maximum, descends into the staggered minimum and climbs the maximum the bracket stands on, ending AT the bracket

scene_composition.describes: ethane in the Newman view, entering at exactly the pose STATE_4 settled on (348° and 108° are the same arrangement — the rotor is threefold) and turning through eclipsed and staggered to the eclipsed arrangement at 240°
the complete torsional curve, drawn in the first 900 ms so it stands still while the rider moves

the barrier bracket spanning the PUBLISHED low (staggered, 0) to the published high (eclipsed, 12); it draws only once the curve is complete, and prints 'barrier 12.0 kJ·mol⁻¹' beside the span. Its x is engine-derived (plot midpoint + 96 px = φ 239.38°), so the SWEEP is authored to end on the extremum it draws at: rider x 480 px against bracket x 479 px on the 700 px plot — one x, one yellow emphasis (measured note item 5, Rule 32e)
the rider crossing 12.0, descending to 0.0 and climbing back to 12.0, settling ON the bracket's upper arm — the peak it measures is the peak the molecule just climbed

value-only HUD 'barrier = 12 kJ·mol⁻¹', constant. The live energy line is deliberately omitted: at the pinned instant it also reads 12.0, and two lines printing 12 for different reasons is a degeneracy
the on-canvas delta cue 'The barrier: 12 kJ·mol⁻¹'
the φ row, shown but disabled; the handle tracks the traverse

tts_sentences.text_en: The bracket runs from staggered up to eclipsed.
That height is the rotation barrier: 12 kJ·mol⁻¹ of torsional strain.
It is the edge a rolling pencil lifts over.

STATE_6.title: One formula for the curve
STATE_6.motion_delta: the declared contrast to STATE_5's climb: the rider leaves the eclipsed maximum and drops into the third staggered minimum, so the pinned molecule is staggered where STATE_5's was eclipsed

scene_composition.describes: ethane in the Newman view, leaving the eclipsed arrangement STATE_5 climbed to and settling in the staggered arrangement at 300° — the same picture the molecule showed at 60° and at 180°, one and two full periods back, which is the state's point
the complete torsional curve, no bracket; the third period of the profile is the region the rider crosses, and the 60° x-ticks let a teacher read the repeat off the axis
the rider leaving the eclipsed maximum at 240° and settling in the staggered minimum at 300° — E back to exactly 0.0, the third identical minimum of the turn
the ONE formula surface of the whole concept (Rule 34b), math-serif Unicode: E(φ) = 6(1 + cos 3φ) kJ·mol⁻¹. It re-anchors to the top-left because the graph owns the bottom-left
value-only HUD 'φ = N.N°' and 'E = N.N kJ·mol⁻¹', so the formula's two symbols both carry a live number
the on-canvas delta cue 'The pattern repeats every 120°'
the φ row, shown but disabled; the handle tracks the traverse

tts_sentences.text_en: One formula covers the whole curve.
The 3 in cos 3φ repeats the pattern every 120°.
The dot drops to the third minimum: same energy again.

STATE_7.title: Turn it yourself
STATE_7.motion_delta: ONE motion with ONE driver: φ free-runs at 24 °/s and wraps forever, its own slider handle sweeping with it, until a teacher grabs that slider and takes the coordinate over; the sandbox never freezes (Rule 37)

scene_composition.describes: ethane in the Newman view, turning continuously; one full turn takes 15.0 s and one 120° period takes 5.0 s
the torsional curve with its stationary labels, no bracket and no formula — the sandbox surfaces core-ring content only (Rule 38b)
the rider circulating over the curve, or following the handle the moment a teacher drags φ
value-only HUD 'φ = N.N°' and 'E = N.N kJ·mol⁻¹', both live under the teacher's hand
the on-canvas delta cue 'Turn it yourself'

three LIVE control rows: View (Standard / Along the bond), φ 0–360 step 1 — the control that NAMES the visible motion, seeded from the driver at t = 0 (60) and tracking it live at 24 °/s until a trusted drag seizes the coordinate — and Show hydrogens. The implemented 'spin' row is deliberately NOT exposed: it drives a rigid turn of the whole picture about the view axis, a second driver for a motion the eye cannot tell apart from the torsion, and its 'Turn speed' label would name a rotation it does not cause (measured note item 7). These three rows ARE the state's discoverables — no unrendered annotation carries content

tts_sentences.text_en: Turn it yourself. Drag the angle φ to any value, switch the view, or hide the hydrogens.

field_3d_config._cameras_and_endpoints_are_MEASURED_note: Do not round or tidy any camera number or sweep endpoint below. Every figure was re-measured on the SHIPPED renderer functions (orgBuildGeometry / orgCamBasis / orgMinScreenGap / orgCamScheduleAt pulled into node, isotropic screen units camX/camZ and camY/camZ, never NDC). (1) dist 8 on every Newman state: at the engine default 11.5 the eclipsed frame's closest drawn-disc gap is +0.042, BELOW the engine's ORG_HOME_GAP_FLOOR of 0.12 — front and back hydrogens fuse at exactly the moment STATE_3 exists to teach. dist 9 gives +0.140, dist 8 gives +0.198, and +0.198 is the worst case anywhere over a full turn. (2) STATE_1 camera az 272 / el -14 / dist 9, sweeping φ 12 → 80. RE-SOLVED 2026-08-10 against the solver's FULL acceptance set, not the disc-gap metric alone, after the eye walk measured the shipped az 180 / el 6 rendering C1's three projected C-C-H arcs as 81.4 / 176.9 / 86.0 and C2's as 104.4 / 148.3 / 42.6 at its pin — a tetrahedral carbon reading as a flat T in the opening image. Achieved at az 272 / el -14 / dist 9, at EVERY φ of the authored window and not merely at the pin: min drawn-disc gap +0.1496 (floor 0.12, cleared by 25%), worst minimum projected arc 105.0°, worst best-arc error 0.79° against 109.47°. At the pin φ = 80 the arcs are C1 116.4 / 110.3 / 145.1 and C2 133.1 / 110.0 / 108.9 — two splayed tripods. THE WINDOW IS THE PRICE, AND IT IS NOT NEGOTIABLE DOWNWARD: an az × el × dist sweep (4 distances × 180 azimuths × 31 elevations × 72 dihedrals) proves the two criteria are JOINTLY UNSATISFIABLE over a full turn — the pose that keeps eight discs countable through 360° is near-axial, which is exactly the pose that flattens the projected bond angles, and the best pin inside the whole full-turn-countable set is still 91.6 / 179.4 / 92.1. The countable arc at this pose is [8.50, 82.75]; 12 → 80 sits inside it with ~3° of margin at each end. Do not lengthen this sweep without re-running that solve. (3) STATE_2 camera_steps[1] el -35.2644 = -asin(1/sqrt(3)), the pose orgSolveCamera returns for sight_along C1-C2, invariant in φ; any other value ends the flight off-axis and makes every later angle claim false. camera_steps[0] is STATE_1's pose VERBATIM (az 272 / el -14 / dist 9) — if item 2 moves, this moves with it or the S1 → S2 click teleports the camera. The flight from this pose never fuses two discs: worst gap +0.0788 (the shipped flight's own worst was +0.0677, so this is an improvement), against -0.2137 for the widest-window candidate az 264 / el 8, which is why that candidate was rejected. (4) Sweep endpoints are chosen so that NO TWO CONSECUTIVE STATES PIN IN THE SAME SYMMETRY ORBIT. Ethane's methyl rotor is threefold with six identical hydrogens, so φ and φ ± 120 render IDENTICALLY: the shipped 358 / 120 / 240 pinned STATE_4, STATE_5 and STATE_6 on the same picture (STATE_5 vs STATE_6 differed by 0 pixels). Now STATE_3 pins at 0 (eclipsed), STATE_4 at 348 (≡ 108, twelve degrees off eclipsed), STATE_5 at 240 (≡ 0, eclipsed — its claim IS the barrier, so it must pin on a maximum) and STATE_6 at 300 (≡ 60, staggered — the formula state needs no maximum). Each state ENTERS on the pose its predecessor settled on (348 ≡ 108; 240 = 240), so nothing teleports at a click; only the pinned poses differ. Twelve degrees is the measured separation floor, not a taste: rasterising the drawn discs, the shipped 2° offset changed 794 cells, 12° changes 3928 and full separation saturates at 4014, so 12° buys 98% of the maximum achievable difference while keeping STATE_4's rider within 19 px (10 px as displayed) of the drawn curve's right-hand end. A sweep landing on exactly 360 MEASURES as 0 and would snap the rider to the left edge of a complete curve; 348 also avoids that. (5) STATE_5's sweep ends at 240 because that is where the ENGINE draws the barrier bracket. orgDrawGraph fixes the bracket at bx = clamp(X(midpoint) + 96, L0+30, R0-30) on a 700 × 460 plot with L0 = 92 and R0 = 674, i.e. x = 479 px ≡ φ 239.38° — a peak the shipped 0 → 120 sweep never visited, so the state showed two yellow emphases at different x and broke its own causal claim. X(240) = 480 px: instrument and rider now share one x to a single plot pixel (half a pixel as displayed), one glow focal, Rule 32e. If the plot geometry ever changes, this endpoint must be re-derived from bx, not left at 240. (6) STATE_2 was retimed from the skeleton's ease_ms 9500 / pin 11300 to 12500 / 14300 so the three claims it carries fit at 2.55 words per second (chemistry block §I-3, founder-accepted). (7) STATE_7 exposes view / phi / implicit_h and NOT the implemented spin row. torsion.continuous 24 and the spin slider drive two different rotations that look the same in the Newman view — the dihedral, and a rigid turn of the whole projection about the camera axis — so the shipped state rendered a molecule turning at 24 °/s beside a row reading 'Turn speed: 0 °/s'. One visible motion, one driver, and the control that names it: the φ row is seeded from orgPhiAt(t = 0) = 60, tracks the measured dihedral live at 24 °/s, and a trusted drag seizes it. Do not re-add spin without giving it a label that names the rotation it actually causes. Every scheduled key is STEMMED (phi_at_ms / phi_ramp_ms / reveal_at_ms / reveal_ramp_ms); a bare at_ms is authored ONLY inside the measure array leg, which is the one place the frozen-pin evaluator reads it.

regeneration_variants.label: The same rotation one carbon along: propane about its C1–C2 bond
regeneration_variants.physical_world: Propane replaces one of ethane's six hydrogens with a methyl group. Sight down the C1–C2 bond and the same Newman picture appears — three spokes from the centre point, three from the rim — except one back spoke is now a carbon.
regeneration_variants.same_physics: Identical reasoning: one rotatable single bond, a threefold profile with minima at staggered and maxima at eclipsed, and a barrier read as the height from one to the other. Only the size of the number changes, because one eclipsing pair is now H against CH₃ instead of H against H.

regeneration_variants.label: A hexagonal nut turning on a bolt, one flat at a time
regeneration_variants.physical_world: A spanner turns a hexagonal nut. The nut can stop anywhere, but let go and it settles with a flat against the spanner's jaw; getting from one flat to the next means lifting over a corner.
regeneration_variants.same_physics: A rotation with a periodic energy profile: six equivalent low positions, six barriers between them, and a period set purely by the symmetry of the turning object. Ethane's methyl group is a threefold rotor rather than a sixfold one, so its period is 120° instead of 60°, but the shape of the argument is the same.
